description: PyBatteryID identifies battery models in a linear parameter-varying representation using Python. The Eindhoven University of Technology developers provide model-structure, regression and voltage-simulation functions, with examples of excitation design. Users supply battery capacity, sampling interval, open-circuit-voltage versus state-of-charge data and informative current-voltage measurements, optionally including temperature. Model coverage is a tested battery and its experimental operating range, with temporal resolution set by the supplied sampling period. The fitted models can support storage-system and electric-vehicle simulations. The package is free under BSD-3-Clause and offers LASSO and ridge-based estimation choices. A limitation is its reliance on sufficiently informative experiments; the README warns against expecting accurate identification from arbitrary drive cycles or unsuitable pulse tests. It also avoids extrapolating the electromotive-force curve outside the provided state-of-charge range. The tool complements physical battery models with a fitted dynamic representation. No battery data were downloaded and no model was identified or simulated.
name: PyBatteryID battery model identification
